question: A started a journey at 1:00 p.m. at a speed of 40 km/h. B started from the same spot and in the same direction at 1:40 p.m. at a speed of 50 km/h. How many minutes will B take to catch with A?
solution:
**Given:**

Speed of A while starting the journey at 1:00 pm = 40 km/h

Speed of B while starting the journey at 1:40 pm = 50 km/h

**Concept Used:**

Time = (Distance)/( Speed)

**Calculation:**

⇒ Distance covered by A between 1:00 pm to 1:40 pm = (40)/(60)times 40

⇒ Distance covered by A between 1:00 pm to 1:40 pm = (80)/(3)km

⇒ Relative speed of B = Speed of B – Speed of A

⇒ Relative speed of B = 50 – 40 = 10 km/h

⇒ Putting the values in the formula,

⇒ Time = (frac{80)/(3)}{10}=(80)/(10times 3)

⇒ Time = (8)/(3)hrs

⇒ Now, convert hours into minutes by multiplying it by 60,

⇒ (8)/(3)hrs=(8)/(3)times 60=8times 20=160 minutes

**Therefore, B takes 160 min to catch A with his speed.**
